metadata.title: Nvidia Signals AI Financing Flywheel Will Continue, But ‘Disciplined’: Analyst Calls Neoclouds Its ‘Biggest Sustained Bet’ As NBIS, IREN, MRVL Rally

content.text:
Nvidia Signals AI Financing Flywheel Will Continue, But ‘Disciplined’: Analyst Calls Neoclouds Its ‘Biggest Sustained Bet’ As NBIS, IREN, MRVL Rally
-
Nvidia reported Q3 results above expectations and raised its fiscal 2028 sales forecast.
-
NBIS and IREN rose over 10% in overnight trading, while CRWV gained 9%.
-
"The Neoclouds aren't a nice to have for $NVDA. It's the biggest sustained bet," said analyst Daniel Newman.
Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) on Tuesday said it will continue supporting the AI infrastructure buildout through investments and credit guarantees, albeit with a "selective" and "disciplined" approach, easing a key concern AI investors had after former CEO Jensen Huang's exit.
Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress highlighted neocloud operators as an important part of the AI chain and its continued support, but clarified that credit backstops activate only if partners can build and deliver the computing infrastructure.
Neocloud, AI infrastructure, and chip stocks rallied on the disclosures, buoyed by Nvidia's strong quarterly results and outlook. Nebius (NBIS) and IREN ltd. (IREN) rose over 10% in overnight trading late Tuesday, while CoreWeave (CRWV) gained 9%.
Marvell Technology (MRVL) gained 5.7% and Arista Networks (ANET) rose 3.7%.
Chip heavyweights Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Micron (MU) and Broadcom (AVGO) rose 2.7% to 4.7%, pushing the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) 3.8% higher.
Nvidia's AI Financing Push
"Neoclouds remain an increasingly important part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem, providing additional customers with access to Nvidia compute and expanding the reach of our platform," Kress said on the analyst call.
"We have supported the development of this ecosystem, and we will continue to be disciplined and selective in our support."
Nvidia has become a de facto financier of AI infrastructure, partnering with and investing in dozens of companies. Huang played a central role in these deals, and his departure fueled concerns that Nvidia might scale back its support.
"As we advance this work, we remain thoughtful in how we participate and disciplined in how we commit capital. We are proud of the role that we have played so far in supporting the ecosystem," Kress said.
"As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees," Kress said.
Nvidia disclosed $32 billion in neocloud commitments, down from $36 billion in Q2, and $118 billion in total guarantees. The chipmaker reported $390 billion committed toward future supply and capacity, up from $279 billion a quarter ago. Nvidia said the uptick was "primarily related to the multiyear procurement of memory supply," the company said.
